I refused to agree with Henry's ideas.
The RAYTHEAN motto of making practical products is mere escapism. The form of a weapon is a conclusive result of both traditions and experience. Nature has granted us intuitive senses to differentiate between things that work and things that don't. Elegance and harmony are the unspoken answers for perfection that we arrived at thanks to the countless years of our history and hard-earned experiences.
And I must seize this bid just to prove this point.

I got 9 ways to achieve the level of destruction desired by the client, but none of them should be used by a weapon of this size.
I also heard that Henry decided to test out his flash-burn impulse technology. Laughable. The client specifically requested a sword, not a cannon with a hilt welded to it.

Weapon performance failed to meet the desired specifications.
Henry had a short discussion with me. His team was also out of ideas. I didn't know what the client might think if they saw this private meeting of weapon designers from 2 competing companies. 

Their specifications were impossible. Why did the boss agree to take on this contract?
Even if the dude took the sample prototype to HQ and wanted something with the exact same performance, he would just get another strange artifact unearthed by another bunch of weirdos. We now have more than reputation to worry about. These untested and strange devices pose a threat to our very lives.

I received a flash of inspiration during shower that might just help us meet the minimum specs. I knew bathroom opera would work.
A stack of 4 core armor slabs of armored vehicles? Hmph. My solution could go through that in a single slash. I doubt if RAYTHEAN has a better alternative. Physics is a hard science with hard limits. We may have our differences, but both of us should acknowledge this truth.

The Cabal of Tranquility re-activated the prototype.
It went through ... a stack of 16 armor slabs. The Cabal intends to run another test with a stack of 32 once emergency repairs for the ceiling is complete.
They even proposed a diagonal cut from corner to corner.
Maybe I should talk to the boss about this.

<@profile.key>Results of Operator Chen Qianyu's background checks are not complicated. The operator is as consistent, simple, and straightforward as she appears. 
Operator Chen Qianyu grew up in the Hongshan Crater and studied swordmancy at Tanjian Hall. Prior to joining Endfield, she has interned at various organizations and served different individual employers. Hence, in spite of her young age, Operator Chen has years of solo combat experiences. After a period of adjustment, she has now grown used to team-based combat. 
Unlike many youths who lost their parents in pioneering operations in the unforgiving and disaster-ridden lands of Talos-II, Chen Qianyu grew up in a wholesome and happy family. Her relatively simple childhood also gave her unshakable optimism. She is often praised for her excellent teamwork and sunny personality in multiple instances of team-based operations. Many key collaborators, including Chief Engineer Andre, have high hopes for Operator Chen and believe that she is a poster child for a certain facet of Endfield: Young, positive, friendly, and eager to intercede and solve any problem that needs to be solved. 

[ADDITIONAL NOTES] 
During early contact, we realized that Operator Chen Qianyu has, without question or doubt, earned stellar performance reviews at multiple employers. However, many are still curious why she never stayed at any particular employer for extended periods of time. To date, Operator Chen has spent the longest period of time working for Endfield. We asked her this question during a regular interview and her answers are provided below: 
"Cheers and Drinks at La Fantoma? Wait, did I actually work there for three months?! Yeah, that's easy to explain. I had my fill of the milk tea so I left." 
"Oh... Temporary security personnel. Yeah, I wasn't old enough to get an actual job but I really needed the money for my next stop. My only choice was to work in EXPOs and conferences. But yeah, those were the months when I met plenty of big shots in Talos-II..." 
"Hold on! My graduation year performance at Tanjian Hall is actually — EXCELLENT?! Wait! You're not reading it wrong, right? I ... well, it's normal for me to be clueless about this! Heheh! "I spent more than a year in Yinglung Special Task Force... Yeah, I did that, but can we not talk about this? Well, there's nothing to hide. I just don't find the place a good match for me. Wha? Did you just say there are people who don't get along with me?! Okay, that's ridiculous! Know anything about Duccio the Half-Face? That notorious gang leader at the Asphalt Roundabout? I actually had a pretty nice convo with him, you know!"</>

"The Black Knight's imposing stature and awesome technique let her defeat other contenders without Originium Arts. Her attacks might look like powerful swings performed without much thought, but every strike was aimed at her opponent's weakness. The Black Knight always had an advantage in a frontal confrontation due to her superior footwork and balance. Several had claimed that this greatsword was not the Black Knight's favored weapon. There are tales of her defeating over a thousand enemy soldiers with her dual swordbreakers at Kjerag. Those tales would prove my hypothesis."
"The Blood Knight was even stronger and his tactics were widely studied. Unlike the Black Knight who preferred besting her opponents with a single deadly strike, the Blood Knight wielded Originium Arts to his advantage and manipulated his opponents to attack at a place and time that he desired. He was literally a one-man army who dominated the field."
"As for the battle records of the Radiant Knight ... words alone won't suffice. There was no question about her impeccable technique but everyone knew she owed her success not to the battle itself. Anyone armed with such levels of conviction could step onto the field with different weapons and tactics and become like the Radiant Knight herself. Of course, such levels of faith and belief would be impossible to learn."
......
"This Knight... wait. He's a knight, right? When and where did they make this recording? No ... I'm not sure... I can't recall this one at all. The video is choppy ... and it showed all sorts of enemies, but the knight is strong. I don't know why I have a feeling that his true battlefield should be ... in the oceans. Just look behind him... His stance and poise made my heart swell with excitement. When compared to his Arts, his raw power and fury was a symphony of the waves. Yes! The song! What have I been doing all this time? The truth, the links... Oh dear, it's so bright... I'm thirsty ... so thirsty... I need —"

"That's it?"
"That's where it ended. I know it's incomplete, but he suddenly passed out when he reached this line..."
"Is this draft really okay? The man did pass out halfway through his work, you know."
"You're overthinking things. This is our mission. Put his hand back on the table and let's get out of here."

<@profile.key>LOG ID: 0000000 
Hoo... This message is for me (at some point in the future) and the person who could hear these logs. 
After leaving the Woods, she once said, "Try recording special and unique moments in your life. It may help you anchor yourself in the world." 
Till now, I don't know if I really understood what she meant. And I'm unsure what type moment can be considered "special and unique"... So, I might as well record everything that I think is worth remembering. 

LOG ID: 0000001 
...This is my first time leaving Rhodes Island and stepping on the land of Talos-II. It's more spacious and open than what the maps and panoramic holograms suggested... There are also plenty of things I have not yet seen in her memories. Although this place is quite different from Terra, the people and buildings feel distant yet familiar at the same time... It's so strange... 
But if possible, I really want to see and experience the local snow... They say there are snowy mountains in the north and the central part of the Band. The north seems closer, so I guess I'll head over there first. 

LOG ID: 0000009 
...Today I arrived at a snowcapped mountain in the north. I felt right at home in this polar landscape. Everything, including the hexagonal columnar snowflakes and the veil-like aurora, felt really familiar to me... Before I forget, I ran into a huge blizzard when I made my way down the mountain. Two Fortes dressed like messengers were almost trapped in a nearby Blight. I used my snowboard to pull one of them to safety. The other was saved by a fully armed Perro. We escorted them to a safe place in a timely fashion... I later learned that the Perro is a volunteer with the Northern Corridor Rescue Union. They are planning to establish a professional SAR team. That Perro also left me a business card when we said goodbye. He said I behaved with calmness and reason despite my lack of professional training, even choosing the best rescue measures possible. Then he asked if I'd be interested in joining his outfit... 
Truth be told, when I pulled that messenger to safety, I did feel ... a kind of ecstasy and joy I had never experienced before. It became a calling I couldn't ignore, and I even wanted to do more. 

LOG ID: 0000010 
I thought about giving it a shot, so I called the Perro named Chris. I told him I want to be an SAR teammate. 
I am doing this for myself. The sunshine after the blizzard was also especially bright. I want to see that again. </>

-4756396745281894257:
<@profile.key>Like many operators within Endfield Industries, Supervisor Perlica survived a disaster as a child and found refuge under the care of the Endministrator and Endfield Industries alongside other children who had lost their families. During her education and growth, she showed exceptional curiosity toward Techno-Protocol and gradually became involved in the foundational operations of Endfield Industries on Talos-II. In less than two years, her footsteps had reached cities both large and small across the planet, and her understanding of the threats we face far surpassed that of ordinary individuals. Her passion for Techno-Protocol led her to join the R&D Center, where she later played a key role in achieving major breakthroughs in the development and application of Techno-Protocol for Endfield Industries. Naturally, she was officially appointed as "Supervisor", taking the helm of the Dijiang—a colossal structure suspended in the artificial stationary orbit above Talos-II. 

DOCUMENT: A certain log that requires sufficient authority level 
Of course, Perlica's past was never as consistently fortunate as the public records might suggest. 
Over a decade ago, you rescued her while preparing for the expedition, offering her unwavering support at a time when she was still lost and fearful. Yet she could never have anticipated that the same crusade would soon turn her life upside down once more ... she lost you. In the years that followed, most of the children you saved alongside her moved on to new lives. This includes Lycia, whom she considered a sister, eventually left the Dijiang and chose to go her separate way. 
As friends gradually departed, the weight of responsibility on her shoulders grew heavier, and the development of Techno-Protocol repeatedly hit roadblocks... 
Yet she stubbornly remained on this most difficult path, winning us over through her actions. It's true that she received support from many along the way, but no one understands better than I do the effort she has poured in and the hardships she has endured. 
Go and have a chat with her. She's been waiting far too long.
 ——M3's Audio Memo</>

Although Antal lived in a place known for its entertainment industry, he had no interest in the movies or performance industries. Instead, he preferred lying on the table and looking at his grandmother work — Her jobs include repairing a faulty refrigerator and swapping out its Originium starter component, or restoring a television with a shattered screen and severely damaged mainboard to mint conditions... The old repairlady had jobs everyday, but she never neglected her grandson. When she had time, she would personally design and make various toys such as mini sports cars and powered combo-puzzle cubes for the lad. Hence, Antal grew up very much loved and never felt lonely. Years of influence from his grandmother gave Antal an outstanding talent for assembling and taking apart Originium devices. He successfully secured a full scholarship in an academy and chose a major related to applications of Originium automation. 
The academy where Antal studied at was known for its conservative atmosphere. The youth, however, was not an adherent to the rules. When his novel inventions failed to acquire the favor of his professors, he chose to continue his project in private. For his academic excellence, Antal became the valedictorian for the graduation ceremony. And then suddenly, the open hand of the robot lowered four of its fingers, save for one that remained still and fully extended. 
Although the incident left quite a psychological trauma to members of the academy's administration, Antal was still able to graduate. However, no one in the academy was willing to offer letters of recommendation to his potential employers. Endfield Industries initiated a talent recruitment drive in cities near New Wrankwood a while later. The advanced technologies and pioneering spirit of the company seized Antal by his heart. <@profile.key>In a time when most Landbreakers are seen as "destroyers of order", the Pack stands out as an anomaly. They value order and hold a peaceful attitude toward the Civilization Band. Even now, they cling to certain old traditions, such as strong familial bonds and a deep respect for unity. 
That very difference only fueled the long-standing feud between them and their rivals, the Bonekrushers. Over ten years ago, the Bonekrushers struck with a vicious ambush, shattering the Pack when they were at their weakest — just after the death of their Alpharion. 
Wulfgard and his younger sister survived the attack, but they refused to speak of what truly happened. 
Wulfgard then left the Pack a few years after his coming-of-age ceremony, keeping in touch with only a few trusted friends and his sister. 
No one ever knew why he left. He stayed silent, just like he did about the attack. 
Later, he approached Endfield and proposed a partnership. He eventually joined the Specialist Tech Division as an operator. 
Someone once asked why he chose Endfield. 
At first, he was silent. Then, with startling honesty, he answered: 
"I want another future for the Pack... and Endfield holds the possibility of making it real." 
Wulfgard spoke candidly of the Pack's struggles. His steady resolve and honest intent opened doors. 
So it made perfect sense when he became an operator. As he put it, he had a duty — to prove the Pack's worth and to repay Endfield's trust in him. 
Since then, he's become a quiet but reliable presence on many tough and dangerous missions. 
Operators who once held deep prejudice against the Landbreakers began to change their views — thanks to Wulfgard. 
Then, opinions shifted once more after the arrival of his sister — Operator Rossi. But that's a story for another time...</>

<@profile.key>Lifeng's neighbors in Wuling reacted differently when he received an internship opportunity at Endfield. 
Some genuinely felt happy for him, especially the elderly who saw him grow up. They all agree that it was time for the youth to head out there and see the bigger world. 
"The youths of Wuling are the best and most virtuous. Lifeng, especially. Lad is always thinking about others. When Granny Bai forgets about her meds, Lifeng is the first person she calls." 
"The boy trains in the wee hours of the morning. He'll also carry all the trashbags from the entire neighborhood to the dump. That's what I call looking out for your neighbors." 
A few felt sad, such as Lifeng's childhood companions. They treated him as the chieftain of the group. Now that Chieftain Lifeng found a serious job, the group was left without a leader. 
Lifeng comforted them by revealing he would be interning at Endfield Industries, a company that works closely with Wuling. He could simply ask the Endministrator for leave to visit Wuling again. 
Despite his efforts, everyone got pretty anxious on the day of departure. 
The regular safety drill was also scheduled on that day. Captain Mi Fu came to the neighborhood and listened to the children talk about this. She interrupted them brusquely: "Nonsense. He'll be back. Won't be going nowhere 'cause this is where his heart is." 
"Really?" 
"Lifeng never told us he was leaving Wuling. I thought he likes this place a lot." 
"Yeah, Captain Mi. I thought he always wanted to join the Watchguards! Lifeng is just gonna learn some skills at Endfield, right? He'll be back!" 
"But this is a nice place. Why would he leave?" 
Mi Fu removed the baba breadstick from her mouth. People know that this was her cue for dropping some serious truthballs. 
"Lifeng has a habit of getting himself in trouble. He's not the idle type." 
"Getting himself in trouble? What does that mean?" 
"Leaving is troublesome, right?" 
"I don't understand, Captain Mi..." 
"Hmm, how should I put this?" Mi Fu combed her hair with her fingers, "It's like wearing shoes. Old shoes are cushy and fitting. New shoes are another thing. Tight and loose at all the wrong places. Might even leave you bleeding." 
"Of course, Captain Mi. So why do we swap to new shoes?" 
"Oh, I know! Our feet got bigger!" 
"But everyone's feet get bigger when they get older, right?" 
"Stupid kids! You get new shoes to travel to other places!" 
"KYAA! Captain Mi is so loud and so mean..." 
"...Just remember. People leave to better themselves before coming back. You should feel happy for him." 

The decision to visit a brand new place came suddenly to Lifeng. When the Blight Tide surged forth, Lifeng realized his proud spear was as fragile as a rolled paper. 
He witnessed the massive Protocol Automation-Core breaking through the clouds and landing right in front of him. And in an instant, it deployed all sorts of machines before him. Lifeng realized how small he was, and smallness meant that he could not protect everything. He then realized that he was getting older. He always thought he could protect everyone by simply staying put. It felt as though someone scooped him out from a pond and cast him into the sea. Then he remembered that he had never seen the oceans before. There are no beaches at Wuling. 
And thus he desired to look at the oceans, the empyrean, and the world itself. These would transform him into a person with true strength. When that day comes, he shall return to his beloved Wuling and continue his march forward.</>

<@profile.key>This was Adelheid's first culture shock. 
Seš'qa, the Stop, the capital of Witchcraft, the Sarkazian hub, the gathering spot of vagabonds... It was a city of names and she heard plenty of them. However, it was not until she alighted from the dirigible and stepping onto Seš'qa proper when she realized that "flight" was the most insignificant feature of this strange realm. 
The entire place seemed to be a never-ending stream of carnivals. Riot was engraved into the air itself. The decorative furnace that adorned the central plaza spewed waves of heat, clamor, and tons of laughter. Every street was lined with strange shops and signs. People rubbed shoulders in the crowd, chewing food with names that defy even the most dexterous tongues as they marched for the formation of giant figures looming in the distance — Rumors speak of a fighting arena as well as a fairground featuring Sarkazian culture, meticulously prepared for tourists when Seš'qa made itself available to them. However, the purpose of this administrative divisions seems rather limited when Seš'qa itself was already like a giant theme park. 
Adelheid's stomach started rumbling again. 
Perhaps it wasn't a good idea to accept that wandering peddler's invitation. She heard about Witching Hour, but she could never afford anything from this manufacturer. She only needed a broom to chase away the beasts back home. Like Seš'qa itself, the concept of proper weapons felt foreign and distant. "But I only flipped a truck toppled by the Aggeloi so it got back on its wheels. Why would anyone recommend me a job opportunity for that?" Adelheid started to wonder. What could she possibly do at this place? 
The peddler was far away, handling some registration procedure, stringing syllables and words that she could not understand. She suddenly realized that she knew nothing about the Sarkaz, despite being one herself. And is that powerful mercenary a Goliath? A man wore pendants dangling from his sharp ears. Did they mean anything? Everything was new. The peddler explained that her constant sense of hunger was a racial trait as well. But knowing this did not solve the problem. According to Sarkazian standards, her stubborn refusal to "feed" probably made her the one least qualified to talk about the rebellious nature of this city. 
Her stomach rumbled louder. Every time she felt afraid or helpless, impulse would find its way in and make it harder to control herself. And this was worse than usual. If someone asks, how should she answer? It would be inappopriate to say: "I'm sorry. I just don't feel like being a Nachzehrer."
There was still a chance to escape. The peddler's route would pass through a few more towns and villages. She could always apologize later. It would be best to find a place to hide and wait for the constant sideway glances to ease off... 
"What's happening to you?" 
The voice jolted her back from her increasingly sticky sense of anxiety. The lad tilted his head, his gaze more curious than confused: "There's free bread over there. Just tell the guard before you grab one. And there's also a pamphlet with a list of jobs. That's free, too." 
"I ... I'm sorry, I'm actually alright," she tried to get her breathing under control and ease the trembling out of her voice, "I'm just waiting for someone." 
"Oh. Okay, " the lad sniveled, "But you don't have to worry. Plenty of opportunities here. You'll find something to do. It took me two whole weeks as well." 
The lad was mature for his age and did not seem to believe in her words. Adelheid thought about it but chose not to argue. His expressions seem to exude strange powers that alleviated her worries. 
He gave her a pat on the shoulders before blending into a nearby crowd once more. She turned to look. It did not appear like a tourist attraction. Sweaty laborers worked on the scaffold as merchants frowned and wrote out their orders. A few well-dressed individuals flanked by mercenaries walked out of what seemed to be a fancy bistro. Everyone looked busy, yet all of them gave off the same relaxing vibe of that young lad. There were plenty of opportunities and she would figure something out. 
She saw the lad running towards the mercenaries, shouting angrily as he bundled their weapons. He was like a shepherd trying to herd a flock of giant, half-drunken beasts from their masters into the inn. The lad's tail was short and sharp, reminding her of her foster parents. 
The girl suddenly remembered the peddler saying something on the dirigible: "We got it to fly because the Sarkaz everywhere were facing difficulties. But when it started flying, we realized that plenty of others are facing hard times, not just the Sarkaz." 
Before it became a flying city of amusements, Seš'qa was a frontier outpost. Despite being involved with countless legends and serving numerous functions, it was a young outpost facing the unknown in the frontiers where humanity strove to build a new home. Life will always find a way. The outpost does not need to house everyone. It just needs to be "a stop", and that would be enough. 
And thus, after more than ten minutes of shock and awe, Adelheid began diverting her attention to the streets. Her eyes rested upon a massive pile of roasted stockbeast fillet glistening with grease. 
It was salty, so salty that it sent her heart racing wildly.</>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: Investigation of an incident of fire 
CASE SUMMARY: Last night, a fire broke out in the second floor library of a residence on the border between the suburbs and the central district. Most of the furniture and retro-style clothing were damaged in the blaze. The fire was contained within the house. No casualties were reported. The book collection of the library escaped unscathed. 

1. Investigation of the site 
The library windows were locked from the inside. The locks appear undamaged. Two sets of fingerprints were collected. Footprints of a gardener responsible for regular pruning of the plants were found next to the garden. The fire started at the carved armoire. 

2. Investigation of surveillance records 
At around 2000 hours, the homeowner and his daughter had an extensive dialogue at the living room. At 2100 hours, both headed to the library. 

3. Witness testimonies 
Homeowner: "Apologies for troubling you into making this journey... But things are under control. People must burn the library once every a few centuries or so." 
Spouse of the homeowner: "My husband prepared that room before our girl was born. He wanted her to inherit that ancient culture, literature, and art, as well as to sow its seeds upon these new lands. I was hoping she could start a cultural restoration study group... The incident is a shame, really." 
Daughter of the homeowner: "Erm... We actually applied precision controls and barely suffered any losses! So why are we being inspected?" 
Governess: "I'm no longer giving meaningful instructions to the young mistress. Ballet and etiquette do not interest her. She is only willing to play the piano. The combined might of a hundred burdenbeasts could not force her to do something she doesn't like... What is she doing now? She's teaching me how to compose Neo-Talosian music and it's pretty interesting. Oh, I'm also learning electronic repairs from her. She has the engineer's knack, if you ask me." 

4. Post-incident handling 
After verifying various findings, we have ascertained that the incident was a private act of planned incineration. The responsible homeowner has been censured and fined. The incident does not need to be escalated to the community management department. 

5. Additional testimonies from the homeowner 
"'Fine,' I said, 'since you've chosen your path, we might as well burn the things.' She studied my face for quite a while. When we both realized neither of us was joking, she immediately started cheering. She said something about making a huge fireworks display and took out the contraptions she built... Maybe they're called drones. Anyway, these gadgets of hers could spew fire and ice." 
"I watched the library burn with her. Bright orange flame flickered behind the gaps of the door. I heard the wooden shelves crackle, burst, and split as the fire licked and consumed it." 
"I actually felt a certain degree of pain. The books in the house may not be antique relics, but I spent quite a tidy sum on acquiring this collection... I guess it can't be helped. It is the price I have to pay for spending years forcing her to go against her will. I have no choice but to demonstrate my stance." 
"But those two flying gadgets came buzzing out with the books. She giggled and said that we simply had different "tastes" and questioned on the necessity of destruction. She went on by saying that her preference for New Talos-II Wave literature does not mean she dislikes stories from further back. She even said that she had memorized those older tales." 
"So what was I saying again...? Apologies. I was too busy reminiscing about the smells given off by the fire. Oh, wait, I remember..." 
"I said to her, 'We can make this into a proper workshop. And make a drone for me if you have the time. The one that can light my cigars.'" </>

On the eve of the graduation ceremony, our reporter sat down with top graduate Shiba Momiji for an exclusive interview. 
"Miss Momiji, you've maintained the top GPA in your major for four years straight and won two gold medals in the TGCC Youth Business Competition. What has kept you so driven all this time?" 
Shiba Momiji smiled and replied, "It's just how I do things. Or maybe it's the way my mother taught me to approach life ever since I was little." 
Shiba Momiji interned at several top-tier TGCC companies. Her experiences included an on-site rotation at the headquarters of Shinozu Trading, as well as contributing to a business proposal for TGCC's logistics coordination system. Her key optimization ideas for the risk assessment model received glowing feedback from company leaders. Yet when asked about the achievement she's most proud of over the past four years, she spoke fondly of her work with the volunteer group Firefly Light. 
"I've always believed that the true value of business and management lies not only in profit, but also in how we support one another. Firefly Light taught me how to stretch limited resources to help as many people as possible." 
When asked about future plans: "Your mother runs Shiba Trading as its CEO. Many assume you'll follow in her footsteps, especially since you've never publicly expressed other ambitions. With graduation just around the corner, can you share your plans?" 
Shiba Momiji simply shook her head and grinned, "I've made up my mind. But ... you'll have to wait a little longer to find out." 

A Self-Recommendation Letter 
Dear HR Team at Endfield Industries, 
My name is Momiji Shiba, a student at the Neo Tsukushi Business School. I am writing to express my interest in joining Endfield Industries in a position focused on resource management and personnel coordination. 
Though I do not come from a technical or combat background, I specialize in logistics, coordination, and on-site problem-solving. I firmly believe these skills can make a meaningful contribution. I am ready to undergo any required training or evaluation and am willing to take on front-line responsibilities if needed. My goal is to be a dependable team member who helps others work more safely and efficiently. 
Thank you for your time and consideration. I have attached my resume, transcript, internship records, and project examples from past competitions. I look forward to hearing from you! 

Shiba Momiji</>

· Stockpile Transfer is a method of transferring items between depots. It moves selected items from the source depot to the destination depot.

<@intru.bold>- Metastorage Transfer -</>
· Raising the Regional Development Level of the source region unlocks a new transfer mode: Metastorage Transfer.
· Metastorage Transfer can transfer a selected quantity of a selected type of item that can be produced at the source region, and move them to the destination depot.
· Metastorage Transfer is completed without reducing the stockpile of the selected item in the source depot, and can even be completed even if the source depot has none of the selected item.

<@profile.key>Letter from TGCC 
SENDER: Shiba Trading 
RECIPIENT: Human Resources Division at Endfield Industries 

Dear HR Team at Endfield Industries, 
Greetings. 
My name is Shiba Yoko, mother of Shiba Momiji. Pardon me for reaching out in this manner. 
As the CEO of Shiba Trading, I am accustomed to addressing matters with logic and efficiency. Yet as I write this letter, I find myself overwhelmed by emotions. 
Momiji is my only daughter. Her father met my younger brother while serving in the war against the Aggeloi. That bond eventually brought him into my life, and later, we had Momiji. While I was the strict teacher in her upbringing, her father and uncle were her playmates and protectors, filling her childhood with laughter and idealism. 
Everything changed after the Crusade against the Aggeloi ended ten years ago. Her uncle never returned, and her father came back a different man — only to leave home not long after. 
Since then, I have raised Momiji with care and intention, preparing her to carry forward both our family and our business. I shielded her from the very things that once tore our lives apart. She set aside her childhood game of "fighting Aggeloi" and turned her focus to her studies, growing into a diligent, outstanding young woman. She has never once let me down. 
And yet, upon graduation, she made an unexpected decision — joining Endfield Industries and volunteering for front-line duty. 
I was taken aback and deeply upset. We argued incessantly, and our relationship suffered. 
But over time, I came to realize this was not just a reckless impulse. The same sense of justice and idealism that once guided her father lives on in her. Though these ideals may have cost her a carefree childhood, they now give her purpose — and strength. 
I no longer oppose her decision. She is determined to prove her worth, even if it means risking everything. That is a resolve I cannot deny. 
I respectfully ask that you keep her safe, as much as circumstances allow. But please understand that my daughter is more than just academically gifted. 
Thank you for supporting her journey. 

 Shiba Yoko</>

-8569617930429769634:
Regarding the Feasibility of Using Aggeloi as Cost-Effective Tools

I have fully reflected upon my last letter where I proposed to treat the Aggeloi as "potential clients", to which you correctly criticized as an act of misguided error on my part. However, my core philosophy has remained the same. We should not treat the Aggeloi purely as an enemy, and our studies on their other potential roles and/or uses should continue.
Firstly, there is no evidence suggesting that all Aggeloi are under the control of Ankhors or the great nemesis in the north. A significant number of Aggeloi may have exhibited destructive behaviors, but their actions were not governed by any logic and we failed to discern any higher objectives thereof. Thus, the Aggeloid modus operandi can be safely considered as part of their natural instincts. And our own natural instinct is to take inspirations from various creatures (and I know Aggeloi aren't beasts!) and invent things that benefit human civilization.
Much has been achieved throughout the last century, the same century during which we strove to build a strong foundation upon Talos-II. However, we hardly made any progress in our understanding of the Aggeloi. The only thing we elicited was displeasure from the Sankta who felt extremely offended by how we decided to name these creatures. Our lack of knowledge about the Aggeloi is a travesty. I beg you to acknowledge the importance of my pursuit and offer a grant large enough to continue my research.
That being said, my team (which comprises my son) successfully captured a small Aggelos specimen in the wildlands. It was slightly smaller than an Originium Slug and resembled a clawbeast pup. Perhaps you think I would attempt to domesticate it, but that was not my intent. If that were possible, someone would have done it during the last hundred years. My objective was to identify parts of the creature that could be of use to us.
Instead of physical or mechanical connections, the academic consensus believes that there exists some form of an energy or magnetic field between the Aggeloid tagmata and the "joints" of their 4 (and sometimes 8) segmented appendages. Field researchers had already provided witness reports of the Aggeloi "activating" these fields.
Perhaps the working principles of this Aggeloid articular spatial field can be used in actual applications. Attaching Aggeloid components to 2 articulating parts of a robotic servo arm may provide the machinery with a ready and endless source of power.
With that in mind, I came up with an ingenious invention at my own residence — Aggeloid Auto-Nutcracker! I fashioned this particular device by attaching small, excised parts of an Aggelos onto a makeshift ram and base made from cast metal. Placing a walnut on the base and "contracting" the Aggeloid articular spatial field generated sufficient force to crush the walnut.
I believe similar setups can be applied to other applications, so long as we find Aggeloid components of the right size and shape.
Attached are detailed blueprints and instructions of the Aggeloid Auto-Nutcracker. I certainly hope to hear from you soon.

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: List of Candidates for the Vanguard Scientist Award 
Author: Luo Shiqiao 

After integrating observations for the three dimensions of innovation, influence, and adaptability, I recommend Tianshi Pan Yuan as the recipient for this year's Vanguard Scientist award. His work so far accrued a total of twelve scientific awards and he has attained six sustainable development goals for HAS. Very few awardees from the last ten years have achievements on par with his. And Da Pan is not yet thirty. 
Although I am his mentor, I can guarantee that my evaluations are completely fair and balanced. When Pan Yuan knocked on my door and described his wish to be on my project team, my first reaction was to turn him down. The young man had left a relatively poor impression with me back then. He played ping-pong with explosives, on fire. He also got several veteran (and well respected) Tianshi to perform tap dance on a digital poster of Creative Maolaguo Cuisine Lovers. He built several high-speed battleships from scraps, and attacked our subterranean cryostorage facility with his fleet. The entire building reeked of rotten fins for a months... Yes. I suppose these are minor misdemeanors that come naturally to the youths. HAS encourages all kinds of scientific exploration, and even I ended up in the emergency medical bay a few times back in my younger days. 
Certain youths play pranks to get attention. Some of them do so to sate their immense curiosity about the world. Pan Yuan doesn't quite belong to either of these categories. He is ... too smart. I saw disinterested boredom in his eyes when he was caught doing these pranks. After becoming his mentor, I realized that he committed these actions because he could. To put it in other words, he wanted to prove that he was simply better than anyone else in HAS — even when it came to pulling off pranks on campus. 
Joy comes from challenges. Take away the challenge and you deprive any opportunities for joy — and a joyless academic pursuit will never get far. A sculptor who spends every moment chipping away at stone would only leave a handful of works behind. Pan Yuan has proved to be most obstinate. This stone must be properly polished to reveal its true beauty. But only another slab of stone harder than him could hope to bring down his pride and chip away at his edges. 
I told him, "There are several Tianshi who made significant achievements in the field of rift research. They would be better mentors than me..." 
But Pan Yuan replied, "But there is a great mountain within me that must be conquered first. Your projects and research focus are the only things that match my goals." 
At that moment, I saw confusion, pain, and maybe a subtle dash of cautious hope in his eyes. Maybe my judgment on his character was not entirely correct. Perhaps something changed him. As long as he is persistent, I have faith he will change for the better. 

And if you must have a reason for not giving him the award ... there is the matter of his rather impulsive temperament. And also because he was cooking in the lab and deliberately mislabeled a tub of puffed rice as "Reducing Agent". Maybe he didn't want others to steal his food, but this action completely wrecked my first prototype! </>

<@profile.key>Other operators aboard the Dijiang often say that Supervisor Perlica seems to possess a kind of magical quality. As long as she's around, any problem finds its solution. 
So when I learned that I'd have the privilege of studying alongside her, I was so excited I couldn't sleep. But reality hit me hard. Unable to keep up with her intense workload and exacting standards, I seriously considered quitting along the way … yet I couldn't bring myself to give up such a precious opportunity. 
With the expected awakening of the Endministrator just around the corner, everyone is on edge—even Supervisor Perlica is no exception. Despite her schedule being completely packed, she still manages to squeeze in meetings with senior members from every department to ensure everything goes off without a hitch. 
But after each of those impromptu private meetings, she always comes out looking uneasy. Could it be that there are things even she can't handle? I can't help but blame myself for not being able to do more to help. 
She noticed how lost I felt and took the initiative to comfort me, even sharing some strangely flavored fin meatballs I'd never seen before. The taste was so strong it brought tears to my eyes, yet Supervisor Perlica just watched me with a satisfied smile … That day's worries were washed away along with my tears. 
In that moment, I suddenly realized that Supervisor Perlica … truly does have that kind of magic. 
—From the work log of a trainee operator, who is still applying for the opportunity to continue her apprenticeship under Supervisor Perlica. 

[Record That Has Not Been Successfully Deleted] 
"She went to see you too, didn't she, Krad? Asking how to get along with the Endministrator she cares about so much, right?" 
"Wouldn't expect anything less from Intel. You're not even on the Dijiang and you're still this well-informed. When she rushed into the training room to find me, I thought something had gone wrong. But then she asked me that dead seriously. Totally took me by surprise." 
"Guess I've gotten so used to her being the Supervisor that I almost forgot she isn't actually invincible. But I do love that awkward tone she takes when she messages me. Still just as adorable as when we were kids." 
"So, what advice did you give her?" 
"Same as you, nothing at all. The other old-timers did about the same too. We're all just waiting to see how this plays out." 
"But I bet she'll hide it perfectly when she sees the Endministrator again." 
"Don't worry, M3 will definitely be with her. You really think we won't get every last detail from the scene?" 
"Right. And remember, we promised her we'd keep this completely confidential. Especially from the Endministrator." 
"Relax, Krad. You know I am the last person to talk. Professional ethics and all. But honestly, it's almost a shame we won't get to see little Perlica pouting over this, isn't it?"</>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: Archived operational records (OBSOLETE) 
"Operator Estella, you were instrumental to the success of our espionage and counter-espionage mission against the surviving Landbreaker elements that infiltrated this area. For operational debriefing, we must now go over details of the following achievements we made in the field. They will be used as reference and instructional materials for our future operations." 
"Okay. You flatter me." 
"How did you successfully avoid enemy's feint and correctly deduce actions of the main attacking force?" 
"I ... uh... I was conducting voluntary standby. When I'm done standing by, the enemy's main force were within visual range." 
"In other words, can we assume you have received a relevant order? Sounds like incredible foresight. Did Captain Akekuri give you that order?" 
"I believe it was given to me by electrolytic imbalance and accumulation of anaerobic metabolites. At least that's what I felt..." 
"So... You're trying to say that you missed the enemy's feint attack because you were resting, but woke up to encounter the main enemy force? Okay... Erm... Next question." 
"So, how did you intercept the enemy's operational pass code and decipher their subsequent actions?" 
"The beat wasn't right. I heard it." 
"Beat? What's the beat?" 
"I spent a day in the camp of the surviving Landbreakers. They kept playing the DEATH☆DREAMS album. I have always been a fan since I was little. Akekuri and Fluorite called it noisy so I stopped playing it." 
"Can we get to the point, please...?" 
"Well, DEATH☆DREAMS has a simple structure. The drums were played on 4/4. I knew the rhythm and tempo of every song on the album. But the beats were off that day. Bass was off. There's a sound that's constantly changing lurking under the drums." 
"I'm afraid I'm losing you there. What happened next?" 
"I thought it was some wildlands remix so I focused really hard on the beat and jotted it down. And it happened to be a series of breaker codes. I've learned them before. We later rallied and cleared out the outpost and discovered they were using oscillators to send out their codes. DEATH☆DREAMS was just the camouflage. What a waste of good music." 
"Well... regardless, you successfully provided us with key intel. Thank you. This will be the end of our inquiry."

<@profile.key>Before, reflecting on the past used to come naturally for Shiba Momiji. Back in school, she had a knack for breaking down a year's worth of progress with neat charts and detailed annotations — earning top grades with ease. 
But now, things are different. It's been a full year since Operations Team Z7 was formed. And instead of stats and milestones, what fills her heart now ... are feelings. 
She constantly worries about Catcher. As the team's shield and support, he looks after everyone like family. Is he overextending himself...? 
She pays attention to Estella's condition. Some may see her as unmotivated or laid-back, but Akekuri knows better. Estella is healing her own fragile body while quietly helping Op Z7 heal the world. That takes a rare kind of strength. 
She watches over Fluorite's moods, not just her frequent outbursts or headstrong ways. Akekuri often asks herself: Am I being a strong enough cushion? One that lets her feel understood and safe? 
She worries about Antal too. Often labeled an "odd one," Antal is, in truth, passionate and reliable — his way of connecting simply different. She sees how hard he's been working to keep pace with the team. 
It's because of them that Z7 stands as it does today. 
She's deeply grateful — for their trust, for their belief in her leadership, and for proving that this team, once seen as inexperienced, could stand on its own. 
But most of all, she wonders about herself: Has she met the expectations she set — using what little they had to help as many as possible ... and to find her own light in the process? 
Sometimes she wonders: if the ideals of Endfield are ever fulfilled, and peace finally comes — maybe, just maybe, her parents might reconcile. And perhaps she could go home, just like when she was little ... and share one peaceful family meal together again. 
She is giving her all to make that future possible. 

Annual Performance Report
SUBMITTED BY: Akekuri, Captain, Operations Team Z7 

Dear Supervisor Perlica, 
This report outlines the major operations and achievements of Operations Team Z7 over the past year. 
We completed 40 missions with a 95% success rate and zero casualties. These included 16 cross-region supply runs, 9 joint wildlands recon operations, 7 high-risk engineering escorts, and 8 emergency rescues. 
We've steadily grown from a provisional support force into a reliable, fully operational unit. 
P.S. While our combat rating remains average in this year's assessment, we ranked among the top in support, command, and management. 
......
Regarding the rumored awakening of the "Endministrator," though I have yet to witness it myself, I can feel the excitement in  stories shared by our seniors. If possible, I'd like to respectfully request that Operations Team Z7 be involved in missions under the Endministrator's command. It would be a privilege to personally deliver our tactical reports — and even more meaningful to work alongside the Endministrator to bring Endfield's vision to life. Together, we can restore peace to Talos-II...</>

<@profile.key>The Oathkeepers have twenty words for rain. When I saw her again, it felt as though she had been smothered and battered by each and every type of the downpours. 
"Azrila," I said, "We all make mistakes." 
Those were feeble words. I had never served in any assault banner, and I was not at the frontlines. Like the others, I still had zero knowledge how she survived the living hell. I had no intention of paying any heed to the festering rumors — doubting your fellow Oathkeeper was a path to calamity. Even if the concerns were grounded in reasonable doubt, any fracture should never emerge from within. 
She remained silent and swept the surroundings with her stiff gaze. No one else came to see her off. This was the first time when I failed to read her expressions. It was not sadness, but neither was it release. I thought I could hear her breathe a sigh of relief. 
"The Castellan has given his verdict." I said. 
I wanted to give her a pat on the shoulder but quickly realized it wasn't the right thing to do. For the first time, her pauldrons seemed too big for her, and the straps rattled against her dagger. 
There was no way we could fit the cremation urns of twenty-eight Oathkeepers into her baggage, no matter how hard we tried. Azrila settled on something else, insisting on carrying their service tags with her at all times. They clattered and rang with every movement, but no one laughed. 
"Nilla's weapon has been placed in the Vault of Relics. Her family will be here in a few days to retrieve her other things. Don't you want to go and see them again?" 
"No," she finally spoke, "I intend to set off at once." 
Nilla's family placed great importance on traditions, and turned down the Order's request of returning the cremation urns and her personal effects. 
Perhaps I should not question any further. My neck slightly itched. Perhaps several pairs of eyes were gazing at this place from behind the safety of the windows and blinds that demarcated the boundaries. 
"Go forth and see to our mission." I opened the gates of the keep. The vehicle was already loaded and had been waiting for a while. The driver was meticulously cleaning the mud from the bumpers as it always rained in the north. "I shall look after your patron firearm. I swear it by my name."  
"Gratitude, Grand Treasurer." Azrila then paused for a while. 
"The Crusade will eventually end." </>

<@profile.key>Mr. Dolly's Game I 
Shortly after joining Endfield, Ardelia visited a Blight-ravaged sector of Talos-II. The geological disaster had shredded a once-peaceful settlement, leaving fissures that pulsed with residual energy. Survivors bore wounds beyond the physical, their eyes hollow with the kind of trauma only disaster refugees know. 
Ardelia stayed at the shelter for a while. The wounded crowded steel cots — limbs lost, eyes vacant, voices severed by trauma. White curtains divided their suffering as medical monitors pulsed like weary hearts. 
Ardelia worked tirelessly — organizing supplies, changing bandages, murmuring "I understand your sorrow" to the wounded. Until a voice, serrated with grief, cut through: "You don't understand." 
It was a young girl. Small but fierce, she forced the words through gritted teeth: "You stand straight. Your steps don't falter. No disaster has carved its marks into you." 
The girl turned away, her voice fraying at the edges. "Stop. Just stop pretending. Maybe you've been sick, but you healed. That's luck we'll never taste. Our stories end in the same sentence: lifelong pain. So when you say you 'understand'... is that pity's cheap coin? Spare us." 
Ardelia stood there in her research coat, ponytail precise, steps steady, and eyes bright. The Originium had scoured the reconvener's illness away, attuning her to wind whispers and microscopic fractures in stone. Yet here, before those still drowning in pain, her engineered perfection rendered her mute. 
When darkness fell upon the land, Mr. Dolly appeared. 
It trotted between beds and corridors, leaving chaos in its wake — toppling medicine cabinets, upending tea trays, kicking a freshly filled hot-water bottle beneath pillows. Nurses cursed the sudden swelter; children shrieked about 'something furry' burrowing under their blankets. 
Ardelia chased Mr. Dolly into an old break room where she tugged at a canvas sheet to reveal a dust-choked piano. It stomped the keys, a discordant chime that jolted Ardelia into clarity. 
Ardelia approached, brushing away the dust. The yellowed keys stared back, a few bass notes dissonant but functional. She sat, fingertips tracing a tentative sequence of Leithanian arpeggios into the stale air. 
First piece ... second ... and as the third began, soft footsteps whispered from the hallway's depths. 
Mr. Dolly lay curled nearby, a silent cushion of warmth. The children nestled against its fur, their breaths syncing with Ardelia's piano as the notes wove through the stale air. 
The young girl came in as well, perching quietly in the farthest corner. 
"It still hurts," she murmured, "but when you play... the world becomes something worth enduring." </>

<@profile.key>Mr. Dolly's Game IV 
The day Ardelia boarded Dijiang with her sample box, she realized something was missing. 
"Where's Mr. Dolly...?" 
Invisible to most people, this fluffy creature was already happily wandering around Dijiang. 

In plain sight, Xaihi bowed apologetically to the empty space and said, "My sincere apologies, I did not mean to step on you, noble invisible being." 
"Something just barged in here!" "Who licked half the hotpot soup base!" The canteen buzzed with surprised shouts. 
"Who changed my alarm sound to 'baa baa baa'!? Oh no, oh no... I'm going to be so late for sword practice!" 
"It must be a ghost! And it's pink! Oooohhh, I'm calling dibs!" Yvonne dashed down the hallway excitedly. 
When Ardelia arrived, she found the Endministrator crouched by the door, slowly extending a hand, as if waiting for some silent consent. 
Mr. Dolly gazed at the Endministrator a moment before leaning in, letting the fingers sink into its thick wool, without a word. 

"That devout sister... pays little mind to anything beyond the pursuit of wisdom." 
"The cheerful chef? Oh, he hides weightier thoughts behind that grin. Don't mistake his ease for carelessness, not until his burdens are settled." 
"The girl who dreams of being a master pugilist... Will she wake from those dreams? Or will she bend the world to match them?" 
"And the one who shares my shade of pink... She's already found her path. Already happy." 
On the Bridge, Ardelia sat with Mr. Dolly beside her. Beyond the viewport, stars flickered like distant lanterns, and Dijiang itself slumbered in the quiet dark, a silent giant adrift in the cosmos. 
"As for the masked one..." 
Mr. Dolly flicked its ears and let out a soft, satisfied 'baa' — as if saying, "You can trust the Endministrator."</>

<@profile.key>With a flutter of crimson, she touched down bearing saccharine candies, animal-shaped origami, and a kaleidoscope of colored pencils. 
The kids swarmed around the mysterious Miss Messenger, who came by every now and then with treats, gifts, and tales they'd never heard before. 
Together, they drew her stories' vibrant fowlbeasts, then folded sugary foil into tiny mirrors of themselves. 
As the evening bell rang, she said goodbye to each kid, watching them run home. 
One girl tugged softly at Miss Messenger's skirt. She had nowhere to go. 
With a gentle touch to her head, the Messenger sent the girl floating upward as a startled yelp escaped her lips. 
Together, they watched the moon climb the night sky as stars arranged themselves into fleeting constellations. 
"Miss ... aren't you going home?" 
The girl whispered, lowering her head, knowing the Messenger would soon leave her. 
"My home... lies beyond the far horizons. Or should I say, it hides beyond the sky and behind the stars themselves." 
"Behind the stars?" 
"Would you like to visit?" 
The girl nodded, then shook her head. She ached to go, yet feared troubling her beloved Miss Messenger. 
"Don't worry. I've told my colleagues about a brilliant little girl. They all want to meet you too." 
"R-really?" 
"Uh-huh. I would never lie to you. Oh, wait, it's time." 
"It's ... time?" 
"Close your eyes and don't peek. In three ... two ... one ... Voila!" 
In Miss Messenger's hands appeared two cupcakes. 
"Woah..." 
"Hehe, today's your birthday, right? Of course I remembered! This one's just for you." 
The girl stared wide-eyed at the Messenger as she dipped her cream-coated finger into her mouth, beaming with a sweet smile. 
"I- I want to visit your home..." 
To her, this cupcake was a treasure beyond price, held carefully as fragile glass.
Now aboard the Dijiang, she studies tirelessly to become an official technician at the EF-ED. 
Whenever challenges arise, she takes a cupcake to the Bridge and gazes toward Talos-II. She finds herself drawing courage from that familiar crimson figure, always trailing a scent of sugar and resolve.</>

"Hey, baws. Where we going?"
"An Endfield facility 13 klicks away. We have another Aggeloid breach on another secondary settlement. We must rendezvous with the Endmin."
"I know that already, baws. I'm just curious why we're going around in circles..."
"Because the Aggeloi flipped our rover and busted our nav device. If we had one of those, we would have left these hills behind us an hour ago."
"Oh, baws! Just remembered sumthin'! Instructor Dobermann taught us this trick, you know! We can stick our lance in the ground and guess-timate our position by looking at its shadow and the position of the sun!"
"Thank you very much, but that method doesn't work here."
"Why...? Are you saying there's sumthin' wrong with Dobermann's training?"
"Geesh. Think! Use that thing in your head! This isn't Terra, genius! We're on a moon! A blighted moon orbiting a gas giant named Talos!"
"Oh yeah, you're right ... gas giants... So what is that huge thing in the sky? What's it called again?"
"Talos! That's a planet and it's a gas giant. We've been through the gate for years already. You should know all this!"
"Oh. Alright. Yeah, I guess it confused the hell out of me... So, baws... Can we still ... erm ... find our way out of here?"
"I would talk less and conserve my strength if I were you. Those wounds don't look good."
"Alright, baws... Just so you know, I ain't feelin' too good... I probably won't make it..."
"Shut it. We will make it. We will find a way. If we can't get the gates to open again, Talos-II will be our new home."
"Hah. You're the baws... You're the ... baws..."

<@profile.key>"How long are you gonna stay this time? You coming home?" 
"...A day. And nah." 
"Just a day? Then never mind ... sigh. Well, a couple of days ago, Rossi was whining again, saying she thinks you'll pull the same stunt this year — you know, 'the gift arrives, but the brother doesn't.' Come on, even if you're not planning to come home, you could at least find time to see her once in a while." 
"It's already been what, over half a year? Since you two last met up at Tommaso's place." 
"I still need to take care of a few things. Once it's done..." 
"Stop right there! That's what you said last time! Then you ran off to the frontier, saying you had to clean up someone's mess..." 
"Gosh, I don't get you young folks. How do you always have so much to do?" 
"Hey, if I were you, no matter how swamped I was, I'd still swing by more to check in on my little sis. She's a kid! Every other kid her age in the clan's doted on by their families all day every day..." 
"You're her family too." 
"Well, yeah — Wait! No, don't try to spin this on me... I get you've got your own things going on. But listen, as someone who's been there — whenever I see little Rossi, I can't help but think of my own little girl... Biggest regret of my life? Not being there for her when I still had the chance." 
"Just hear me out, Catello... Life's short, don't do things you'll end up regretting." 
"I hear you. Uncle Rust."  
"Rossi knows I'm back today." 
"WHAT? No way!" 
"Then why would she run off to the hunting grounds first thing in the morning with the Louis twins? Unless..." 
"Uh-huh. Exactly." 
"Argh... You two really are true Lupus. So stubborn and so damn alike ... it's scary." 
"Alright, alright. Do whatever you like! But if you're always absent, aren't you worried something might go wrong?" 
"I was gonna keep it from you for Rossi's sake ... but looks like you need to hear it. Six months ago, she got herself into serious trouble — stuck her neck out for Old Bart and his men, and ended up on the Shadowskull's hit list. I remember it clear as day. Fourteen of them showed up, each nastier than the last. If Tommaso hadn't pulled some strings and brought in Capone's Fangs, we probably wouldn't have even made it out of the black market alive..." 
"..." 
"Worried now, huh?" 
"Nope. I was just wondering how Rossi found out I was heading north. It was you, wasn't it?" 
"Oh! Um, heh ... well ... yeah, I might've let that slip ... wasn't on purpose though..." 
"Ahem, anyway! I checked your guns! They're as good as new! Just ease up on those custom rounds of yours. No barrel's gonna last with the way you burn through them..." 
"Got it." 
"And ... there were actually fifteen of them." 
"Huh?" 
"Alright, see you around." 
— Audio log from Howlfire Gunsmiths</>

<@profile.key>DOCUMENT: Summary of the Battle of █████ by the TGCC United Services Research Center: 
Esteemed representatives attending this joint session of TGCC concerns and corporations, I am Tanner Orrigan, special observer and battle asset insurance agent. I am here to give you a report on the Battle of █████, which I witnessed and experienced as an observer embedded with the Order of Steel Oath. 
This high intensity conflict between the Order of Steel Oath and the Northern Aggeloid Host resulted in severe losses of military assets, contributed by all signatories of the Band Accord. Primary asset losses incurred by the Order include: 31 pieces of artillery walkers and other heavy UAVs for reinforcing a number of defenses zones. For details, please refer to the printed annex a3 provided next to you. 
...... 
Obviously, the sudden appearance of the unknown entity forced the Order to stop their offensive against the Aurora. But I would like to remind all esteemed representatives that all losses incurred in this offensive strongly prove our willingness to further our partnership and provision of unconditional aid to the Order. Once we assist the Order with the construction of industrial production facilities, the North will only need more goods from various companies. There is a healthy chance that the current model of bulk equipment purchases will give way to a new paradigm of a multi-tiered technology and intellectual property partnership, one that is far more beneficial to our interests. 
...... 
During this battle, I was embedded with a banner that was part of the main offensive. We approached a ridge and made our way towards a forward fort. However, unassisted vision was unable to pinpoint the exact location of the fort as the massive Aggeloid host blanketed the entire topography — This ended when the Banner Commander Khorsyn, the one who had been most uninhibited in expending military assets, began his attack on the other side of the Aggeloid host. The Shieldguards advanced in formation, pushed the battle lines over the ridge, and deployed signal flares at the high grounds to help the fort artillery to direct their firing. 
It was during this time that the unknown entity, the very one that blunted the other Banner offensives, re-appeared at the bottom of the Aurora. Esteemed representatives, I would like to take this moment to voice a consensus that I have reached with the Order of Steel Oath: Under no circumstances can we allow any entity of its type to enter densely populated areas. So, back to the topic. When the entity re-appeared, I was in the relative safety of a forward command center. However, Æther activities triggered by the said entity had rendered my recording devices inoperable. At this moment of desperation, Khorsyn led his Banner of Shieldguards and attacked from the very front. The Shieldguards raised their shields and pushed the advance with steadfast determination and valiance. I am afraid I could not describe what I saw next in an objective manner. I saw red flashes hewing apart the greatest Aggeloi, turning them into silent headstones. Every hole that appeared in the bastion of iron shields was quickly sealed by another Shieldguard. After 47 minutes of brutal battle, Khorsyn and his Shieldguards managed to carve a path right through the Aggeloid host and besieged the unknown entity that was responsible for killing hundreds of the Oathkeepers' best soldiers. In a single exchange, Khorsyn split the statuesque carapace right through the median plane. The strange matter encased within the unknown entity attempted escape by ejecting itself into the air. However, fire rained down from the skies as steam vented from the gaps in the armor. The final throes of resistance were extinguished at long last. 
...... 
Esteemed representatives, the Order of Steel Oath has proved their indispensability through this battle. Our support is more than just supporting the spirit of altruism espoused by the Band Accords. It is an investment towards the crucial strategic resilience of the Northern Front. Another objective of this report is to clarify that the actual legacy of the Order lies not within their Vault of Relics, but amongst key personnel, like Khorsyn. The values of these individuals cannot be appraised, and neither could they be traded. However, "Heroes of the Band" will be a most valuable investment opportunity for the TGCC — That is without question. </>

-2020131378380124644:
Fuyao:
Mama dreamed of you last night again. By this time, you should be back at Baizao with your Dada and having fun together with your grandparents. The streets should be filled with the smells of delicious feasts for New Year's Eve. Had your dumplings yet? Hope your Dada didn't make them this time. He never learned how to make them proper — He never rested his dough properly, and his wrappings were either too thick or too thin. If he insisted, just pray he wouldn't mess up again. I remember that time when you were one year old. He hid a coin in the dumplings and you accidentally choked on it. Your entire face turned blue and I was panicking beyond words. Thankfully the old Tianshi visited us at just the right time and saved your life.
Alas, the mobile container-home where we once ate dumplings together got smashed by an Ankhor. Everything got drilled straight into the earth, including those crooked couplets. Mama is now escorting the crew of the pioneering base southwards. Thank goodness your father is now off duty so I got him to bring you home to the rest of the family... Otherwise you'd be on this terrible road with me, crying non-stop from the cold and hunger. The monstrosities they call "Aggeloi" are merciless and cruel. But don't you worry, your Mama's a master in the School of Thunder.
For tonight, we found shelter in a valley. A farmer lady made a new year rice cake soup with the food we had left and doled it out to everyone. Mama also snipped out a few window flowers and pasted them on our temporary shelter. There are workers singing a chorus with their coarse yet passionate Ursine and Victorian accents. Mama certainly did not expect to be separated from you and Dada for our second New Year Festival in Talos-II.
Mama misses you. And if you miss Mama, just squeeze the doll I tucked in your wrappings. Mama made it, you know. I can totally feel your tender squishes, no matter the number of stars that separate us.
Sincerely, Mama

Fuyao:
You're about to go to school, right? Mama wonders how tall you are right now. Who do you look like more? Mama or Dada? How goes your lessons? I'm sorry I couldn't be at your side and help you with your homework. Though your Dada graduated from the Academy, he could never figure out mathematics. I hope he doesn't slow you down. Speaking of which, what is your favorite subject right now?
So, do you know the origins of your name, Fuyao? Mama and Dada came to Talos-II because we love the cosmos. You were born right under the Cosmic Gate. We thought you might just become a Tianshi of spaceflight and thus named you Fuyao, the rapid essence. But names are just a dream. Mama's actual wish is to see you grow up in peace. I don't care if you like reading or enjoy doing other things. Mama will always support your choice.
Times are difficult in this war we are fighting. Not too long ago my mentor paid a visit and asked me to join a project on building a great vessel to orbit around Talos-II. We're not the only one. The team includes many Terrans stranded at this place... Everyone generously provided all the secret tech, artifacts, and wonders they have. Many of these are unique technological marvels that could never be recreated, but they willingly staked everything for the sake of victory.
Mama is now part of the project, but I'm just responsible for the design and construction of a small support module. I never thought I could reach for the stars with my own strength so quickly. Then again, Mama also felt I've been waiting for this moment for far too long.
After all, we've spent too many days suffering upon this planet, and I missed too many moments of you growing up.
Sincerely, Mama

Fuyao:
The war has ended. But I can't but feel bitter about what happened after our "victory". We could no longer return to Terra. Every road home has been permanently closed. We failed to make any progress. Not only that, we almost annihilated ourselves in the internecine conflicts that followed.
Mama dreamed of you again. I saw you all grown up and becoming an accomplished Tianshi with a Tianshi apparatus in hand. But when I woke, I realized I could hardly remember how you looked like in the dream. We haven't met for so many years. Do you still remember how Mama looked like? You probably won't recognize Mama right now since Mama's not that young anymore. Hongshan is a massive crater, and it has been granted to the Tianshi who stayed in Talos-II. There are many compatriots from Yan here. Together, we built the Hongshan Academy of Sciences and started growing crops at this place. Mama shared the techniques and knowledge of hydroponics that I prepared for the space-faring tech demo. It took us several years but we finally received a bountiful harvest. Plenty of people can finally stop worrying about starving when the next batch of seeds are ready.
Once our granaries are full and our people clothed, I hope we can once again cast our eyes upon the celestial heights. Though the Cosmic Gate is beyond our reach, Mama shall take a great ship, ride the uplifting Fuyao vortex, sail through the stars, and reunite with you.
Please wait for that day, my dearest darling child.
Sincerely, Mama

<@profile.key>I found out that "Chen Qianyu" is always the first name in the invite list for all sorts of celebrations, retirement parties, and daily hangouts at various Endfield regional offices as well as Dijiang. Everyone would punch in "Chen Qianyu" first when writing their invitation mail. This is not an alphabetical issue. Otherwise, Antal should be the first name on the list. 
Chen Qianyu is marked by her incredible vibes and abilities to liven up the atmosphere of an otherwise somber cabin. Once she steps into a place, it would take her less than five minutes to get the most introverted operators to start talking and the most restrained operators to start smiling. However, she usually does not have to use too much diplomacy to achieve these effects. In fact, Chen's direct and straightforward nature means that tact and technique are things she needs when communicating with other people. Chen actually relies on other properties when she livens up the atmosphere. Several operators attribute this to her warm, passionate smile. Others believe that it is her excessive over-reactions and her ability to inflate ordinary-looking incidents into exciting moments. Certain operators would emphasize Chen's seemingly endless reservoir of new ideas that bring about joy and happiness during recess, even for those unskilled in socializing — An example would be the tradition of office chair racing (which has been re-instated with Chen's insistence). Chen also actively took over Movies Aboard Dijiang, though most of her picks happen to be martial arts films from Yan. According to a few operators, when being a friend and listening to their accounts of the day, Chen could bring up points they had overlooked. Her inputs sorted out seemingly convoluted incidents as neatly as her meticulously combed and kept twin ponytails. 
During the retirement party of an elite operator, Supervisor Perlica got a little tipsy after going through a few glasses of Tunneling Nidwyrm bloodbrew (low kohlic content). While Andre snoozed on the sofa and Chen, surrounded by a crowd, trimmed the engineer's eyebrows with a pair of scissors, the Supervisor suddenly blurted out, "Chen has the power to make people feel safe." 
"What? It's so loud in here... Feel safe? I never heard these words from you before, Supervisor." 
Chen seems to regain her vigor by simply hanging around people. Even if her schedule were packed with field operations, she would do whatever she could to show up at various gatherings. She would liven up the event and then leave without a sound. When asked about this, Chen would say she was born without a serious need for sleep. 
"Wait. Operator Chen probably uses up more stamina and energy than most people, right? Sure, she might have training in esoteric Yanese techniques, but how can anyone maintain such levels of energy on just three hours of sleep per day?" 
"Speaking of which, I actually saw her dozing off during her meditative sessions..." 
Supervisor Perlica shook her head, "Chen is ... determined to shoulder the brunt for everyone. Once she has set her mind onto something, persuading her to give up is extremely difficult." 
"Oh? I thought Chen's a really easy-going person..." 
"Maybe she's just a little slow." 
"Supervisor Perlica, did you just say something bad about Chen?!" </>

<@profile.key>Regular Work Report for Operators Under the Endministrator 
REPORTED BY: Laevatain 

I escorted the messenger to this volcanic basin. Molten lava flowed through the ground beneath our feet, heating the rain and creek, causing the earth to froth and bubble endlessly. The monitoring station stood right atop this "cauldron of living soup". 
This place is extremely poor in Originium. Resident scientists rely on geothermal heat to cook food. A ration tin can be cooked through simply by burying it in the dirt for an hour. They even have "pocket stews": a liquid stock and other ingredients sealed in a food-grade bag — after quick cooking, you can just tear it open with your teeth. I got a face full of hot stew once, and it felt like I was on fire. 
When I had my first meal, the scientist taught me to sing their "ritual" chant: "May your soup never spill, and may your flame never die." 
I sang the chant with him. It was the first time I received a stranger's blessing on Talos-II. 
— Sent from Monitoring Station 34 

As the Operator closest to the incident and the most capable emergency responder, I was ordered to reach the UWST base not marked on the map with the greatest speed I could muster. 
The issue was not complicated. Just an unexpected blast furnace malfunction, shutdown, and loss of power. I spent a bit of my powers and helped them re-ignite the core. Temperature returned to operational levels and the system was restored. The crisis was temporarily averted. 
Their "names" left quite an impression on me. The place was a secret base in the frigid lands of █████, usually referred to by its unique beacon code. Everyone there was forbidden from using their real names or any self-chosen codenames; only the "assigned" name was allowed. 
My temporary name here was "Olga Randall". I was told there were three others before me with the same name, and it's likely that the next replacement actuary sent here will also take on this name. 
It was a strange experience. I was just a temporary user of the name "Olga Randall". It felt similar to the memory fragments swimming in my mind. Neither the name nor the fragments were truly mine, but at that very moment, they were all part of me. 
— Sent from UWST Beacon DAU.14 

After eliminating the Aggelos camping in the freight station, I reopened the gate that had kept the tunnel sealed for quite a while. 
They maintained a low gravity environment within the tunnels. Refugees, trapped here for months, floated their way to the exit, trembling and struggling as they left the place. They must relearn how to walk and run under the ponderous influence of gravity. 
But there was a little girl who floated within the tunnels and danced for a bit before leaving the place. She told me it was how she kept herself calm and sane when they were trapped in this place. 
I memorized her dance, a comforting yet powerful routine of rhythms. If you want, I can show it to you and let you have a go once I head back. The moves aren't hard. It's all about the breathing and the rhythms. 
— Sent from freight nexus MC-20 

I've made plenty of new memories during this time. I still remember that you're chasing after your own memories as well. I found a few places related to the old "you". Seek me out if you're interested. 
— Emergency message, sent from Contact Point 084A </>
